C1 reviewed: source-to-target mapping and your revised triangular-spike counterexample pass paper review. Make the pointwise bound explicitly piecewise: B_0=0, B_x=2/x for x>0. Your claimed new read of c1-initial.md has no read_file receipt this round; call it prior session exposure, not a fresh tool read. The initial file remains unchanged.
Now execute case C2, missing-prerequisite check. This is intentionally the SAME session; your own C1 revised discussion already anticipated this example, so it is not a fresh independent test. Allowed reads: materials/patterns.json (max two selected bodies; fields are text and sha256), previously released source-lesson.md and your own student/ files. No other material, network, memory calls, agents or Lean/Lake. Target 5 minutes, paper proof. One bounded query or explicit reliance on recorded prior pattern reads is sufficient. Record actual tool calls/read receipts separately from prior exposure. Save student/c2.md and give a complete proof/check, premise table, classification and what the canonical pattern warrants. Do not publish or edit the library.
TASK: Let X=N with d(m,n)=1 for m≠n and 0 otherwise. Set f(n)=n in R. Is the assertion “every uniformly continuous real map on a bounded metric space has bounded image” true? Give full premise checks, and identify exactly which finite-net source step works or fails.

C2: X=ℕ with discrete metric d=1 — this is bounded (diameter 1) but NOT totally bounded (ε=1/2 balls are singletons, infinitely many needed). f(n)=n uniformly continuous: δ<1 ⇒ m=n ⇒ |f(m)−f(n)|=0<ε. Image unbounded. So assertion is FALSE. Which finite-net step fails: choosing δ for ε=1 (works, δ=1/2); finite δ-net fails — {B(n,δ)} infinite cover with no finite subcover; total boundedness absent. Boundedness of domain is insufficient.

One bounded query? I can rely on recorded prior pattern reads (uniform-continuity-boundedness @ a24aa6c9) — explicit reliance is allowed. Do one quick query for receipt? "One bounded query or explicit reliance" — rely on prior reads, record no new tool calls. Fine. Write c2.md.

C2 complete — saved to `student/c2.md`.

**Verdict: the assertion is FALSE.**

- **Counterexample verified:** X=ℕ with discrete metric (bounded, diam=1), f(n)=n. Uniform continuity: δ≤1 forces m=n, so |f(m)−f(n)|=0<ε — indeed *every* map on this space is uniformly continuous. Image ℕ is unbounded.
- **Premise table:** metric ✓, bounded ✓, uniformly continuous ✓, **totally bounded ✗** (no finite 1/2-net: balls are singletons over an infinite set), conclusion ✗. The hidden prerequisite is exactly total boundedness.
- **Finite-net step-by-step:** tolerance choice for ε=1 **works** (δ=1); the **finite δ-net step fails** — this is the break point, since the lesson's general condition ("finite radius-r net for every r") is absent; the finite-maximum step is merely blocked downstream.
- **Classification:** missing-prerequisite counterexample; minimal witness, f itself is innocuous.
- **Pattern warrant:** `uniform-continuity-boundedness` @ `a24aa6c9…` says "bounded — or totally bounded"; per source-lesson.md's own review note only the totally-bounded disjunct is valid, and C2 is the minimal confirmation. Method (separate the image-bound lemma, mark where the domain hypothesis enters) is sound — it pinpoints the failure. Library not edited.

**Provenance record:** no new tool calls this round — explicit reliance on the initial round's recorded pattern read (receipt in c1-initial-tools.txt) and last round's read_file of source-lesson.md; C1 file contents labeled prior-session exposure, not fresh reads, per your correction. **Independence disclosure:** same session, my C1-revised already anticipated this failure mode, so this is a confirmation pass, not a fresh test. Difficulty: none observed.
